newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ jobs data supports case for RBNZ easing -Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ jobs data supports case for RBNZ easing -Cullen.

text.p: Employment data released on Tuesday supported the case for an immediate easing in monetary policy, opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said.
Statistics New Zealand's household labour force survey showed the unemployment rate climbing to 6.4 percent in the March quarter from 5.9 percent in December.
Cullen said the rise, in combination with recent surveys showing declining business confidence, suggested there was room for an immediate easing.

"The Treasurer (Winston Peters) must ensure that any easing is reflected in a fall in the exchange rate rather than a further fall in interest rates. There is little benefit to exporters and the tradeables sector if easier monetary conditions leave the exchange rate unchecked," Cullen said.
